descriptionChirho: Piel: to pay back, requite, or recompense someone for what they have done, whether for good (reward) or evil (retribution), the dominant transactional sense of the Piel stem.
Piel: to fulfill or perform a vow (neder) made to God, a specialized sense distinguished from general repayment by its covenantal/religious context (Arabic أوفى, Swahili -timiza).
Piel: to make whole what was damaged or lost — whether legal restitution for property (Exod 21-22), restoration of what locusts consumed (Joel 2:25), or completing a building/work (1 Kgs 9:25).
Qal stative: to be complete, finished, or ended; also to be whole, safe, or at peace — the intransitive state of wholeness from which the root derives its basic meaning.
Pual passive: to be repaid, rewarded, or recompensed — the passive counterpart of the Piel 'repay' sense, indicating the recipient's perspective of receiving what is due.
Hifil: to make peace or submit peacefully to another party, used of diplomatic or military reconciliation between hostile groups.
Hifil causative: to bring something or someone to completion or to an end — ranging from God completing his purpose to bringing a person's life to its end (Job context).
